title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 180 (Restrictions on powers of Board)

content.overview: Section 180 provides that the Board of Directors of a company shall exercise certain powers only with the consent of the company by a special resolution: (a) to sell, lease or otherwise dispose of the whole or substantially the whole of the undertaking of the company; (b) to invest otherwise in trust securities the amount of compensation received by the company as a result of any merger or amalgamation; (c) to borrow money, where the money to be borrowed, together with the money already borrowed, will exceed the aggregate of the paid-up share capital, free reserves and securities premium, apart from temporary loans obtained from the company’s bankers in the ordinary course of business; and (d) to remit, or give time for the repayment of, any debt due from a director.
content.glance: Special resolution required for: sell/lease of whole or substantially whole undertaking; invest merger compensation other than in trust securities; borrow beyond paid-up capital + free reserves + securities premium (temporary bank loans excluded); remit director debt.
content.study: The Board of Directors of a company shall exercise the following powers only with the consent of the company by a special resolution, namely: (a) to sell, lease or otherwise dispose of the whole or substantially the whole of the undertaking of the company or where the company owns more than one undertaking, of the whole or substantially the whole of any of such undertakings; (b) to invest otherwise in trust securities the amount of compensation received by it as a result of any merger or amalgamation; (c) to borrow money, where the money to be borrowed, together with the money already borrowed by the company will exceed aggregate of its paid-up share capital, free reserves and securities premium, apart from temporary loans obtained from the company’s bankers in the ordinary course of business; (d) to remit, or give time for the repayment of, any debt due from a director. Every special resolution passed by the company in general meeting in relation to the exercise of the powers referred to in clause (c) shall specify the total amount up to which moneys may be borrowed by the Board of Directors. Temporary loans mean loans repayable on demand or within six months from the date of the loan, such as short-term cash credit arrangements, discounting of bills, etc., but do not include loans raised for the purpose of financing capital expenditure. The expression “undertaking” means an undertaking in which the investment of the company exceeds twenty per cent of its net worth as per the audited balance sheet of the preceding financial year or an undertaking which generates twenty per cent of the total income of the company during the previous financial year; “substantially the whole of the undertaking” means twenty per cent or more of the value of the undertaking as per the audited balance sheet of the preceding financial year. Current-law framing: identify the act; apply the undertaking/borrowing definitions; require special resolution; note temporary-loan exclusion.

sections.heading: Sell or Lease Undertaking
sections.body: Sale, lease or other disposal of the whole or substantially the whole of an undertaking requires special resolution. Undertaking and substantially-the-whole are defined by 20% net-worth/income and 20% value tests.

sections.heading: Invest Merger Compensation
sections.body: Investing merger/amalgamation compensation other than in trust securities requires special resolution.

sections.heading: Borrow Beyond Limits
sections.body: Borrowing that, with existing borrowings, exceeds paid-up share capital + free reserves + securities premium requires special resolution, excluding temporary loans from the company’s bankers in the ordinary course of business.

sections.heading: Remit Director Debt
sections.body: Remitting or giving time for repayment of any debt due from a director requires special resolution.

examples.title: Borrowing beyond limit
examples.body: A company with paid-up capital and free reserves of ₹10 crore already has borrowings of ₹8 crore and proposes a further ₹5 crore term loan (not a temporary bank loan). Aggregate borrowings would exceed the s. 180(1)(c) limit; a special resolution is required.

examples.title: Temporary bank loan
examples.body: A short-term cash credit from the company’s bankers repayable on demand is a temporary loan in the ordinary course and is excluded from the borrowing ceiling calculation under s. 180.

hypotheticals.question: Is an ordinary resolution enough to authorise sale of substantially the whole undertaking?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 180 requires the consent of the company by a special resolution for sale, lease or other disposal of the whole or substantially the whole of an undertaking.

distinctions.title: Restrictions on Board powers (s. 180) vs powers of Board (s. 179)
distinctions.left: Specified acts need members’ special resolution

misconceptions.trap: All borrowings need a special resolution.
misconceptions.correction: Only borrowings that take the aggregate above paid-up capital + free reserves + securities premium need a special resolution; temporary loans from the company’s bankers in the ordinary course are excluded.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 180 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the act. II. Apply undertaking/borrowing definitions. III. Require special resolution. IV. Note temporary-loan exclusion. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Act facts; limits; resolution type; precise relief.

examTips: Special resolution for four listed acts.
Undertaking = 20% net worth or 20% income test.
Borrowing ceiling excludes temporary bank loans.
Special resolution for borrowing must specify the total amount.

enhancement.definition: Section 180 requires special resolution for sale/lease of whole or substantially whole undertaking, investment of merger compensation outside trust securities, borrowing beyond prescribed limits, and remission of director debt.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: High-impact capital and asset decisions are reserved to members by special resolution rather than left solely to the Board.
essentialIngredients: Specified total amount in borrowing resolution
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 180 is the member-reservation counterpart to the Board’s residual powers in s. 179.
enhancement.problemApplication: Map the act to a clause; apply definitions; require special resolution.
keyTakeaways: Temporary loans excluded from borrowing ceiling.
